answer: A glacier-monitoring subsidy requires one credential per person, issued after a registrar checks for duplicate enrollment. A cedar team may let many agents wander through data, but each claim must prove its credential and expose a program-and-round nullifier derived from a stable hidden identifier. New keys cannot evade the ledger's repeated-nullifier check. A farm needs more real participants or must defeat registration, incurring recruitment or fraud costs. This assumes the proof binds the identifier correctly and the registrar deduplicates honestly; credential rental remains possible.
